text: Hi and welcome to another episode of This is My Architecture from Mumbai. Today I'm joined by
Aniruddha from Bajaj Housing Finance Limited. Aniruddha, welcome to the show. Thanks Anand,
thanks for inviting me. Excited to be here. Great and what does BHFL do and what's your
role there? We are a housing finance company, we are 100% subsidiary of Bajaj Finance Limited.
We offer a full range of mortgages product like home loan, loan against property, developer finance.
We are present in more than 115 plus locations and our current asset under management is almost
2.5 billion dollar plus and I head the BI and analytics department of Bajaj Housing Finance
Limited. Excellent. Alright, so we are looking at a serverless data pipeline and a data mart
architecture. Can we get into the details of the architecture? Yeah, sure Anand. As you can see,
like we have mainly three layers, extract, transform load and serve layer. So in the extract layer we
have multiple databases like loan origination system, loan management, collections and also
we are getting semi-structured data from external system like bureau. So DMS is configured here to
pull the data from both structured databases and semi-structured you know data. Okay and then putting
it into a S3 bucket which is our staging layer. So you can call it as our data lake because we are storing
all kind of data here for further processing. Okay great. So now that we have looked at the data in its raw
format in S3, what are some of the security services that you are using because as a financial services
company clearly security is extremely important for you. Yeah, definitely. So for that we are using AWS
Key Management Service to encrypt customer sensitive data mainly name, phone number, address, all this
customer sensitive data and apart from that we are also using S3 server side encryption on S3 bucket as well.
Okay. So now that we have looked at the security services, what happens next in the process and transform layer?

So in the processing and transform layer, so we are using Lambda and Glue for the transformation. So Glue is taking data from this S3 bucket, the raw data from the S3 bucket and then in the transformation we
we are using, you know, we are actually implementing complex business rules, data quality checks, error handling, auditing, all these things inside the Glue.

And then after transformation, Glue is again storing data into the S3 bucket in the target format. And once it is transformed, then Glue is also loading the data into the Aurora Postgres, which is our data mark.
And once the data is loaded into the Aurora Postgres, then we have a presentation layer where we are, we are summarizing the data. So we have multiple summarized tables.
So Tableau is connected with this presentation layer. So that it can serve data to the business user in the form of dashboard, analytical dashboard and canned report.
Okay, excellent. So we have seen data coming in from extract process and all the way into the serve layer. Two interesting points that I see here in the architecture is the choice of Glue and Aurora.
Why don't we talk about Glue first? What what made you choose Glue?

I had no intention to take any conventional ETL tool like Informatica or SSIS. So I was looking for a solution where I can process, you know, both structured and structured or semi-structured data seamlessly. And also I can build reusable codes.

So I came to know about Glue like here we can write Python coding and also we can take advantage of distributed framework of Spark. And another good thing is that it's completely serverless. So it's managed service. So that's why I choose Glue as our ETL tool.
So what about Aurora Postgre? What other options did you consider before you chose Aurora?

Yeah, there are multiple options like Red Shipt or we can take SQL Server as well. But the problem was like that for SQL Server, we need to take a license. And as a finance company, we have fairly moderate data volume. But my main concern was the concurrency because we have multiple users who execute concurrent queries in the database.
So considering both cost performance, we choose Aurora Postgre.

Okay. So great overview of your architecture. In fact, going into the deep details about security as well as serverless components. Where do you plan to go next? How do you plan to evolve this architecture?

Yeah, Anand, you know that we are totally data-driven company. So once data is there in our database, so we have a requirement of predictive analytics in different department for business decisions, for risk policies, for credit and operations teams.

So for that we are planning to use SalesMaker. The good thing is that it is already integrated with Glue. The second thing is that we are planning to use QuickSight once it is available in Mumbai, because it will help us to reduce the cost of Tableau.

And third is AWS Step Functions to automate the workflow, because right now Lambda is playing that role. So, and it is a little bit complex. So to reduce that, we are planning to use the Step Functions down the line.
Okay. Okay. I think great explanation of the serverless data pipeline that you have built. I believe you built all of this in three months. Thank you for sharing with us this entire architecture.
Thank you, Anand. Thank you so much. Thank you, viewers, for joining us on this episode of This is My Architecture.
